_meta.source: book/on_the_origin_of_risk (Timlett 2025), Technical appendix I (fractional meta-models, endogenous and exogenous stressors)

failure_modes: An over-stressed system carries many fractions that will never be needed
An under-stressed system has too little prepared to adapt in time
Reading the friction of partly built function as pure inefficiency and removing it
gloss: Partly build responses to possible stressors; the cost of carrying them is preparedness
invariants: Full delivery and no delivery are special cases of fractional delivery
Endogenous stress rises with the amount of partly delivered function
mechanism: Rather than fully building or omitting a response to each possible exogenous stressor, build it fractionally: complete some of the components it needs, such as data carried through two of three pipeline stages. If the stressor arrives, few components remain to change; if it never will, the fraction is removed. Partly built function is an endogenous stress, a carrying cost and a source of friction, but it is also the stored optionality described in {{rejection_cost_optionality}}. The right level of fractional delivery rises with the likelihood of the stressor. It makes the stressor integration of {{residuality_stressor_integration}} cheaper. Fast metrics of endogenous stress, such as today's rejection rate, can signal an exogenous stressor and trigger full delivery.
